PullRequest.Title: editor: cap Fit tab width at 400px so long labels truncate
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #348019

With the default `workbench.editor.tabSizing: fit`, a tab always grows to show its full label. An exceptionally long name, such as a long Windows remote path opened in the Agents window, made one tab several times wider than the editor and pushed its Close button out of view behind the editor actions until you scrolled the tab bar.

Fit tabs now size to their label up to 400px and truncate anything longer with an ellipsis, so Close stays visible. Everyday file names are unaffected: 400px comfortably fits normal names, and only exceptionally long labels are capped.

**What stays the same**

- Normal and preview (italic) Fit tabs keep the same widths they have today.
- `shrink` and `fixed` sizing are unchanged and do not inherit the 400px cap; `fixed` still uses `tabSizingFixedMinWidth`/`tabSizingFixedMaxWidth`.
- Pinned tabs keep their `compact`/`shrink` widths.
- Tab wrapping, Connected and pill tab styles, and Close-button position/reserved space all work with the cap.
- The full label remains available in the tab's accessible name and hover.

The `fit` setting description now mentions the 400px maximum.

## Before and after

Agents window, Windows remote session, Connected tab style, `fit` sizing. The before state reapplies the previous Fit CSS in the same session for a matched comparison.

| Before: the long tab hides Close behind the editor actions | After: the tab stops at 400px and Close is visible |
| :--- | :--- |
| ![Before: the long filename tab runs under the editor actions with no Close button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bff54fc0-ab4b-4877-800b-24dbadd6c8d2) | ![After: the long filename is truncated with an ellipsis and the Close button is visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1aa51181-3bd3-4af2-9b35-578c779b7d93) |

Closing the capped tab directly from its Close button:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5165e186-8f3a-4e91-9c4e-f8695e330469

## How to test

1. Keep the default `workbench.editor.tabSizing` (`fit`) and open a file with a very long name (150+ characters), alongside a few normal files.
2. The long tab stops at 400px with an ellipsis, its Close button is visible, and hovering the tab shows the full name.
3. Normal file tabs look the same as before.
4. Switch to `shrink`, then `fixed`: tab widths match today's behavior, and the long tab is not limited to 400px in `shrink`.
5. Repeat with `workbench.editor.wrapTabs` on: the long tab still truncates within the row.

## Validation

- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts --browser chromium`: 114 passing. New tests cover the 400px cap with truncation across legacy, pill, and Connected styles, wrapping, and Close position/reserved space; unchanged normal/preview widths; preview truncation; pinned `compact`/`shrink` widths; and `shrink` not inheriting the cap. Existing tests that used group widths above 400px to force overflow now use smaller widths.
- `node build/stylelint.ts`: passed.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed TypeScript files: passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- Manual check in Code OSS (Agents window with a mock Windows remote host): the long tab measured 869px before and 400px after, with Close inside the tab and working. Shrink and Fixed widths were unchanged in the same scene.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore editor groups with ordinary, preview, or exceptionally long Fit-tab labels in legacy, pill, and Connected styles.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: handleOpenedEditors creates missing tabs, computes labels, redraws labels/actions, and schedules doLayout on the next animation frame. Browser style/layout must settle before the tab bar is painted; asynchronous decorations do not block the initial tab rendering. The diff changes CSS geometry, not editor-content loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser style resolution, intrinsic text measurement, geometry reads, and tab-bar paint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing collection-wide layout work scales with N tabs and total label text. Cold modern unreserved widths measure each uncached tab once in a batch; warm layouts skip width measurement for cached tabs. Legacy and reserved-action tabs use normal browser layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scheduling, DOM reads, intrinsic measurement, and cache logic ran before. Fit labels previously had no 400px cap; the diff bounds final tab width and restores existing label ellipsis without adding measurement calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for visible tab-bar geometry and the next frame; deferred and coalesced by the existing scheduler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request entry per cold URI/provider after service caching, grouped into one IPC batch per provider per queue flush rather than one IPC per tab. Warm positive, empty, and in-flight entries produce no further fetch. Multiple event-loop flushes can create additional existing batches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical setResource/render calls, URI/provider cache keys, in-flight joining, empty-result caching, batching, and refresh behavior. CSS truncation does not issue provider calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous, off the initial tab-layout critical path; completion can cause an existing decoration refresh and coalesced layout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N open tabs per group, total label characters, and U distinct resource URIs across those tabs; realistic groups can have tens or hundreds of tabs. Decoration requests additionally depend on P registered providers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One pending animation-frame layout per tabs control coalesces successive requests. Intrinsic widths for all uncached tabs are measured as a batch after clearing their maximum widths, then restored. Decoration misses are asynchronous and extension-host requests are grouped per provider by a zero-delay queue; there is no new concurrency or serialization introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing tab labels, icon classes, and path labels remain cached. Modern unreserved Fit widths are cached per live tab in --tab-sizing-fit-width, with unchanged invalidation on label/decoration/dirty/options changes. Decorations cache positive, null/empty, and in-flight results per URI/provider; failed requests can retry after subsequent existing redraws. The new 400px maximum does not invalidate these caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from complete diff inspection and the traced open/redraw/layout/cache paths that no expensive boundary, allocation lifetime, or request multiplicity is added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime timings available; browser intrinsic-layout cost depends on label lengths and group size. Remote model loading or provider-specific filesystem/network/subprocess work is outside the changed CSS mechanism and its scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff bounds rendered widths while preserving the existing intrinsic-measurement and asynchronous decoration paths. This is not evidence of a concrete old performance regression being fixed; the demonstrated Close-button issue is functional geometry.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize editor groups and enable or disable tab wrapping, including terminal tabs adjacent to editor actions and Add Tab controls.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Coalesced doLayoutTabs runs wrapping eligibility, row classification, Add Tab alignment, and scrollbar updates. doLayout computes the resulting title height and requests group relayout only when that height changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DOM dimensions and row offsets, update wrapping classes and CSS properties, and potentially relayout the editor group after a title-height change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing O(N) scans and bounded placement/height checks per coalesced layout; no new per-tab callback, observer, or recursive layout mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same row scans, geometry reads, and height-triggered relayout ran before. Modern wrapping maximum widths used the full row width or toolbar-reserved row width; the diff additionally limits those maxima to 400px.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines visible wrapped rows and available editor area before painting.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N tabs, number of wrapped rows, available group width/height, and resize-event frequency. The new cap can reduce the number of rows occupied by very long labels.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread geometry work within one scheduled animation-frame pass per tabs control. Existing row geometry is collected before last-in-row class writes. Wrapping and Add Tab placement use bounded checks, not an unbounded retry loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cached intrinsic widths remain independent of wrapped-row constraints because getFitTabWidths temporarily removes max-width. Existing row and scrollbar state is updated during layout; the diff does not clear width caches on every resize or add new cache keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the unchanged scheduler, bounded wrapping call flow, and retained read-before-write batching. No concrete evidence of increased layout frequency or collection multiplicity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured frame-time comparison; the exact browser cost of CSS min/max constraints and number of rows is input-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. New CSS width constraints do not introduce a layout loop, extra boundary fan-out, or changed scheduling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover or focus a capped modern Fit tab with transient Close/Unpin actions and without reserved action space.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing mouse-enter/focus listener freezes an uncached intrinsic tab width, updates hover/action state, and browser layout reallocates label space while respecting the CSS maximum.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Temporarily remove the width constraint, resolve computed widths for one tab, then restore the maximum and cache intrinsic width.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One targeted intrinsic measurement per uncached tab interaction, zero repeated measurements while cached; the operation and guards predate the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical single-tab measurement and cache guard existed, without a final 400px cap. Existing managed-hover setup and disposal also remain unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold interaction may synchronously resolve geometry before the hovered/focused state is displayed; unchanged placement on the input path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One targeted tab per mouse-enter/focus event, with text length controlling its cold intrinsic measurement; repeated interaction can occur at pointer-event frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous targeted work on the UI thread for a cache miss; repeated warm interactions do not remeasure the width. No new listeners, hover allocations, or async requests are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: freezeFitTabWidthWithoutReservedActions exits immediately when --tab-sizing-fit-width is present. The cached value can exceed 400px intentionally; CSS clamps its rendered width without comparing the cache against the cap or repeatedly invalidating it. Existing tests explicitly exercise this distinction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from listener and cache-guard inspection that oversized cached intrinsic values do not cause repeated measurements.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cold-interaction latency is unmeasured; no changed frequency mechanism was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The cap does not defeat width caching or create extra hover work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change tab sizing between Fit, Shrink, and Fixed or use compact/shrink pinned tabs.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing updateOptions/updateTabSizing/redraw updates tab classes and schedules a coalesced layout. Pinned-size CSS overrides and shrink/fixed selectors determine the resulting geometry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve browser geometry after sizing-class changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing O(N) tab updates and subsequent layout per explicit sizing change; no new per-item service call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same option-change redraw and layout happened before. Only Fit's CSS maximum changes; shrink/fixed rules and pinned sizing overrides are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Needed to display the requested sizing mode; scheduling remains unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N tabs per affected group and frequency of explicit settings changes or pinning operations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous class/redraw updates followed by the existing per-control animation-frame scheduler; no changed limiter, queue, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing redraw and relevant option changes invalidate per-tab width caches; no new cache state is retained. Shrink/fixed tabs do not inherit the Fit cap, and pinned compact/shrink sizes retain their overrides.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from CSS specificity, sizing-class assignment, and updateOptions call-path inspection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Setting changes are user-triggered and unprofiled; no scaling amplification appears in the changed code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Configuration-description and stylelint-variable changes are metadata-only; added test loops are not product runtime work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all five changed files and every diff page. Inspected tab layout scheduling, intrinsic-width caching, wrapping/relayout, hover measurement, label rendering, and cached/batched decoration IPC. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression found and no concrete performance-regression fix eligible for blame provenance. Static review; runtime performance magnitude remains unmeasured.
